_comment: What the audio stack is, as data both implementations are held to.
The exclusion rule is duplicated by hand in assets/omarchy-router
(is_excluded_client) and Model.js (isExcludedClient), and the two had
drifted: they held identical name lists while disagreeing about which
names to reject, so comparing the lists proved nothing. These cases are
the shared expectation -- assets/omarchy-router selftest and
scripts/model-test.js each assert their own implementation against this
file, so changing one side alone fails that side's own suite.
'excluded' is what both must answer for the given (appName, binary).
Matching is EXACT on the tag-stripped name. There is no namespace or
prefix rule, on either side, and that is deliberate. A first-word rule was
here to cover stack names not yet seen; it could not be tested against any
name a real session reports, because every one of them is already on the
list, while still being free to over-match -- and it did. 'PipeWire ALSA
[app]' is PipeWire's wrapper for the ALSA client of an application, and the
bracketed part IS a real installed app (cliamp, a music player, on the
machine that reported it). Treating the pipewire namespace as plumbing
deleted that app from the panel. The 'why' on each case records which side
of that line the name falls on, so the same mistake cannot be re-derived
from a plausible-looking example again.

name only, capitalised, no binary to fall back on. Every other case that capitalises a stack name also carries the lowercase binary, so this is the one that fails if case-insensitivity is dropped
